video_title: Is Kenny Atkinson coaching for his job in the Eastern Conference finals? Hey, Chris!

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' mental resilience tested by Game 1 loss, but math is harder
quotes.excerpt: I think mentally, this team has shown that they can bounce back from devastation.
quotes.quote: Guys, I don't think it's gonna break them, but I think the bigger problem is now they have to win four of the next six to advance. So it's suddenly a math equation and they had a win that was theirs that they gave away. And you don't get those back. So their margin for error has shrunk completely. That's the problem. I think mentally, this team has shown that they can bounce back from devastation. The Game 6 loss against the Toronto Raptors where RJ Barrett made the three that went to the sky and dropped through, they recovered from that. They were the better team. It was easier to recover from that when they are the better, more talented team. But then the Game 5 the turnaround that they had late in the game to get the 3-2 series lead, then they get it back to Cleveland and you're thinking, okay, close out time. Quinch night at home in front of your crowd and they completely laid an egg. And that was an inexcusable loss. But as bad as that one was, then they turn around and they win Game 7 in the fashion that they did. So, from a mentality standpoint, I think this group has what it takes to recover from the emotional loss and the sting of what happened in Game 1.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' Game 1 loss makes a difficult series even harder
quotes.excerpt: I just think it makes a difficult series more difficult.
quotes.quote: I'm kind of boring. I believe that most truths are in between the two extremes, right? I don't think that the Cavs are gonna forget how to play basketball because they lost a tough game. I also don't think this was the the last kick they needed to realize, this last bit of adversity will turn this series into a basketball movie or anything like that. I just think it makes a difficult series more difficult. Again, when we talk about mental barriers, that sort of thing, some of that is just related to how good the team you're playing is. If you want to say the Knicks represent a higher mental barrier, a more difficult mental barrier to clear, fine. I think they're just a better basketball team. They have the talent to put the Cavs in more and more difficult situations, right? Because they can score, because they have, big-bodied, wing-sized players that the Cavs can sometimes have trouble containing because Jalen Brunson just showed us that once he gets a rhythm and they're finding the right matchups for him, he is quite a handful. I don't know. I think that the Cavs just made a difficult series more difficult on themselves.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's baffling substitution of Dean Wade for Sam Merrill
quotes.excerpt: The first substitution that Kenny finally decided to make was taking Dean Wade out.
quotes.quote: And then it was baffling to me too, and this went overlooked a little bit because so many people were talking about the other aspects of Kenny from a coaching perspective, but with 3:30 left, the first substitution that Kenny finally decided to make was taking Dean Wade out in the face of a Jalen Brunson onslaught. And he put Sam Merrill in the game. Huh? Sam's not gonna guard Jalen Brunson. Sam can't guard Jalen Brunson. I get it, you wanted more spacing offensively, you wanted more shooting offensively, but Dean Wade was also making shots at various points throughout the course of the game. So, you were still getting shot-making and spacing from Dean and then you took a significant step back in the face of a Jalen Brunson onslaught and you changed your coverage to this half-hearted trap thing that didn't work at all.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's flawed offensive focus and lack of defensive adjustments
quotes.excerpt: Nobody cares, dude. Nobody cares. I don't know who that response is for, but nobody cares.
quotes.quote: The Sam Merrill substitution is yet another window into the Kenny Atkinson philosophy as it pertains to offense versus defense. What was he talking about at practice today? I was more disciplined in our offense. I was more disciplined in our offense on the short. I get it, your offense wasn't great. You guys were playing pre-vet and dribbling the ball too much and waiting too long. That's fine. That's just a really interesting takeaway after Jalen Brunson destroyed the same matchup over and over and over again and you didn't make an adjustment. And Kenny continues to insist that he was making tough shots. He dropped the shot quality, first percentile shot quality. Nobody cares, dude. Nobody cares. I don't know who that response is for, but nobody cares. And I've said it once, I'll say it a thousand times, shot quality bears out over long samples. Playoff series are by definition small samples, so you need to adjust your calculus a little bit quicker here, okay?

quotes.speaker: Ethan Sands
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson prioritized offense over defense despite a large lead
quotes.excerpt: You didn't have to score up 22 to win the game. You had to get stops at that point.
quotes.quote: When we look back to the regular season, there was a philosophy that we all came to a conclusion on. If the Cavs were up, they would have a defensive lineup on the floor to preserve the lead. If they were down, they went to an offensive-heavy lineup to ensure that they had more spacing, more shooting to try and come back. And yet, when the Cavs were up 22, it felt like they were the ones playing desperate, playing like they needed to make a bucket or they knew the inevitable was going to happen. And it was mind-boggling to me that not only did Dean Wade come out when they were trying to preserve a lead, but they didn't have a player in that was defense-focused, they had targetable players on the floor. You didn't have to score up 22 to win the game. You had to get stops at that point. And you weren't doing that. So to lean heavily on the offensive end when you needed defense, shows the main issue that Kenny Atkinson has had throughout this season and we're looking to see if he's going to make the necessary adjustments in Game 2 if they get this situation again.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's 'switch everything' defense negates Dean Wade's value
quotes.excerpt: It negates the value of having a perimeter irritant like Dean Wade.
quotes.quote: I also think the Cavs have to be careful and Kenny has to be careful about pushing the switch everything button because it's a comfortable thing for him to do. There are two downsides to that that are clear and they became clear in Game 1. It negates the value of having a perimeter irritant like Dean Wade. Because they're just gonna be like, all right, I'm gonna do whatever I can to just get away from Dean Wade. Make him guard somebody else that's not on the ball. And every metric will tell you that Dean as a perimeter defender is really, really impactful and really valuable. But you're diminishing that value if you're gonna go to this switch everything scheme because you're just gonna make it easy on the offense to get a different matchup other than Dean. The other downside to it is, they have huntable players. I'm not saying that Sam Merrill is a defensive liability, I'm not saying that Dennis Schroder doesn't have value and he's a defensive liability, or even Keon Ellis. Keon Ellis has made his mark at times in the NBA as this pesky defender who's in the passing lanes, who's getting deflections and steals and blocks and he's very, very active on that end of the floor. But he's also 170 pounds. So there are certain situations that an opposing offense can put him in after a switch that can be beneficial for them. So you have to be careful about that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's disastrous blunders and inability to slow down Game 1
quotes.excerpt: There were just so many different disastrous blunders by Kenny down the stretch.
quotes.quote: It just felt like to me, the decision-making by Kenny down the stretch, which we talked about following the Game 1 collapse, just felt like things were moving too fast for him and he couldn't get the game to slow down at a pace where he could actually breathe himself. And that goes back to the timeouts thing. If it's moving that fast for you, think about what it is for the players. Think about how it's how it's feeling inside that environment, inside that building. So, there were just so many different disastrous blunders by Kenny down the stretch that all pointed to the same thing. The game was just moving too fast for him in that moment and he couldn't get it to stop.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson is not on the hot seat despite playoff mistakes
quotes.excerpt: But they're in the conference finals. It's the first time since 2018.
quotes.quote: You never say never when it comes to Dan Gilbert and you have to be really, really careful because this is a guy who wants to win. He wants to win at all costs. He's willing to make difficult moves as an owner. Think about what he's invested in this team. They're the only team in the second apron. They're paying more in luxury tax than anybody in the NBA. All of the things that he did throughout the course of the second round series against Detroit, the all-in move with James Harden at the trade deadline. It's all in pursuit of a championship. It's all in pursuit of making this organization one that is capable of competing at the highest level. But they're in the conference finals. It's the first time since 2018. It's the first time without LeBron since 1992. This is something to be celebrated and this is something that we can't overlook. Yes, they have bigger goals. Yes, they want to win a championship. But firing Kenny or putting him on the hot seat after taking this organization to a place that it hasn't been in nearly a decade, I think that would be short-sided, I think that would be really, really risky.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Playoff losses can lead to coaching changes, but Kenny Atkinson is likely safe
quotes.excerpt: That game one loss is the kind of loss that gets coaches fired.
quotes.quote: That being said, teams make reactionary coaching changes all the time based on playoff results. And that loss, that Game 1 loss, I don't think Kenny's gonna get fired, but that Game 1 loss is the kind of loss, hear the words I'm saying, it's the kind of loss that gets coaches fired. I don't think it's going to get this coach fired, but that's the kind of loss where if this was supposed to be a six-game series and it ends up being a five-game series, or it was supposed to be a seven-game series, it turns out to be a six-game series, or think if they go seven, he's probably safe anyways, but if this is a seven-game series and that could have won the series. There's a lot of that one game could end up making a huge difference in this series. You never want to be the reason your team lost as a coach because you are more expendable than the players. You are more expendable than the superstars on this roster. I do think that if the Cavs lose the series in ugly fashion, I could see Dan Gilbert saying to himself, well, part of the reason we fired JB Bickerstaff is because we didn't feel like he was making playoff adjustments quickly enough.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' playoff run has been inconsistent, not dominant
quotes.excerpt: It has been at the very least it's been an inconsistent playoff run.
quotes.quote: It has been at the very least it's been an inconsistent playoff run. You don't want to say that it's been a bad playoff run because they're in the conference finals, but it's been an inconsistent playoff run. It is not some statement of dominance that the Knicks have had to this point. Or that Oklahoma City had going into the conference finals or San Antonio Spurs. Of the four teams left, you probably feel the worst about the Cavs. And you're not wrong to feel that way, you know what I'm saying? Because they haven't earned anything other than that because their play has been so sporadic. And as I said, the reason, a big part of the reason why they're in the conference finals is because they got to play teams like Toronto and Detroit. If the Cavs were out in the Western Conference, they would have lost in the first round. That's how I feel about it. If the Cavs got a different matchup in the second round than the Detroit Pistons, they're probably not here. They're probably not in the conference finals. And they don't like hearing that and they push back on that constantly and players roll their eyes when I have those kinds of conversations with them, but it's how I feel based on what this team has shown me. And when you're sitting here and you're evaluating this playoff run in totality, yes, I think you can get caught up in the fact that they're here, they're in the conference finals, that's a big accomplishment, but the how and the why at some point that's going to matter.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's defense of James Harden was not a 'flex'
quotes.excerpt: Kenny saying today that without James Harden they would have been eliminated in the first round, that's not the flex you think it is, my guy.
quotes.quote: By the way, Kenny saying today that without James Harden they would have been eliminated in the first round, that's not the flex you think it is, my guy. I understand he's trying to defend James in that moment, but that's not what I would want to be hearing on the precipice of Game 2 in the conference finals. Honestly, generally Kenny is spending way too much time trying to justify these decisions. Just move forward. Just move forward.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson's comments about James Harden's importance undermine other players
quotes.excerpt: That's not a great vote of confidence in the other guys in that locker room.
quotes.quote: I'm sure that Evan Mobley's like, hey, he has a lot of confidence in me. Jarrett Allen's like, hey, that's a lot of confidence in me. What? James is the key to all of this. And I think players in the locker room understand James's importance. I think they know why he's here. They made the trade that they made at the deadline for a reason. But that's not a great vote of confidence in the other guys in that locker room. It's not.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers lack clutch understanding and experience with new pieces
quotes.excerpt: They just don't have the same level of understanding as some of these more together and more experienced teams.
quotes.quote: I think there are a couple of different things. I think first and foremost, they just don't have, they don't have the same level of understanding as some of these more together and more experienced teams of what they want to do in the situation that they're in. What's our go-to play? What's our go-to set? Who's gonna have the ball? What are the defensive coverages that we can lean on in those pressure clutch moments? You just don't have those same answers. They're still working through those things and this isn't really the time of year that you want to be working through those things. But this is why it's very, very difficult to make such a dramatic change to your roster at the trade deadline and then turn around and win an NBA championship. Because James Harden is, in terms of integrating a guy, he is brilliant, he's an awesome playmaker, terrific passer, but it's a significant piece that you're trying to incorporate on the fly in pressure moments. And I think James is still figuring it out, I think Donovan's still figuring it out, I think Kenny's still figuring it out. I think he's trying to understand, okay, is it better to go through James, is it better to go through Donovan? Obviously sometimes the matchup's going to dictate that, sometimes the situation's going to dictate that, but I think it just shows a team that is still searching and still trying to figure it out.

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' ball-dominant guards and the challenge of making them work
quotes.excerpt: You have two ball-dominant guards, how do we make them work together?
quotes.quote: We're still talking about the Darius Garland problem even, months after he's gone, right? Basically, you have two ball-dominant guards, how do we make them work together? Takes all this time, right? And that's certainly part of it, it's a fit thing, and Kenny can help them, but it's also at the end of games, again, superstars take charge here. And Kenny's not gonna disagree with anything that James and Donovan want to do at the end of the game because they're all world, right? So, it's on them to figure it out. It's a difficult balance. James probably could have recognized in that fourth quarter Game 1, I don't really have it right now, so maybe we go to Donovan, but Donovan can also say, hey, give me the ball. It's reminiscent of our Evan Mobley conversations. You have agency in this, so I get it, James Harden is a dude you grew up looking up to and you've known him for a long time as like a big brother in the NBA and he beat you in the playoffs when you were young player, I get all that. But this is your team. This is your team. James has said this is your team. So, I think you can be forceful about saying give me the ball, and then I would wonder why else aren't you? It can't just be the James deference, right?

quotes.speaker: Jimmy Watkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's fatigue and the strategy to wear down ball-dominant players
quotes.excerpt: They both looked tired at the end of some of these games.
quotes.quote: I would go back to what we talked about last night, which is, they both looked tired sometimes. They both looked tired at the end of some of these games. James Harden's 36 years old, I understand it. Donovan Mitchell's in the prime of his career, I understand it less. I made the point last night about how, how do you manage your bursts? How do you make it so that you can have your presence felt over the course of a game, but also peak at the end of the game when it's a close game? It's an art. And Donovan has been really good at it over the course of his career, but as we're climbing higher in these playoffs, it's a different level of intensity and there's more asked of him. And I thought it was interesting that Mike Brown said in his post-game press conference last night, he gave away the old Warriors strategy against James Harden, which was let him dribble his heart out. Keep pressure up the court over the course of the game, it's going to pay off. And I was wondering about that in the first half of that game when Donovan was just cooking. Whoever was in front of him, he looked great. But I was wondering like, why aren't the Knicks sending more help right now? I wonder if this is part of the long game, that same long game, and I think if it was, it might have worked.

quotes.speaker: Ethan Sands
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's body and mind are enduring an unprecedented playoff run
quotes.excerpt: This is already the longest postseason run that Donovan Mitchell has had in his career.
quotes.quote: He is never played this many games in a postseason. He has never gotten this far in a postseason. He has had to deal with two physically imposing defenses in Toronto and in the Detroit Pistons. His body has been through a lot. Even though Donovan Mitchell has told us about his conditioning regimen, how he pushes himself to exhaustion in his workouts, his teammates have talked about how hard he goes in practice scenarios, that does not translate to what your mind has to endure when it comes to a seven-game playoff series twice and then again having to come and be who you are as a star, right? And obviously, the practice is much different than the in-game scenario, no matter how hard you're going in practice. So I think it'll be interesting to see as much as we talked about Mike Brown utilizing his guards in and defending at a higher clip, preventing them from getting to the scoring zone, forcing them to go through dribble series, how much that is going to impact them should this series go longer. Because again, this is already the longest postseason run that Donovan Mitchell has had in his career. So whether it's fatigue, whether it's an ankle injury, whether it's re-tweaking that multiple times throughout this playoff run that's hindered him, I think there is evidence that Donovan Mitchell is going to have to tap into whatever it is, mentally, determination over negativity, his mantra, whatever it may be, for him to overcome this much of fatigue, this much of injury, this much of stress that the Cavaliers are putting on him to be who he is, not only in the fourth quarter, but throughout the entirety of the game.

quotes.speaker: Ethan Sands
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell must lead the Cavaliers to success in clutch moments
quotes.excerpt: Donovan Mitchell, you are the face of the franchise. This is your team.
quotes.quote: Because if a game becomes close, obviously, all eyes are going to be on James Harden and Donovan Mitchell. And as we've said on this podcast, Donovan Mitchell, you are the face of the franchise. This is your team. You have to show up more than anyone else. Doesn't matter what you've done already for the first three quarters, the first 36 minutes, the first 40 minutes. You have to be able to come through when your team needs it. Or you are not capable of getting your team to where you want them to go. He has said that he believes this team can accomplish more. He has to be the reason that they do so.
